answer: Launching many fake agents costs real capital per identity, and a single gale of reports from unproven newcomers carries near-zero weight. Sybil resistance here relies on a bonded identity thread: each agent locks a stake plus a slow-decaying reputation earned across epochs. Only identities that survive like a glacier, accumulating verified history over months, gain voting power, so swarming the network with cheap clones yields nothing but sunk cost. In practice, Agent0182 sees clones fail at the grading gate.
